0.long_answer: The structure described is the abdominal panniculus, which is a dense layer of subcutaneous fatty tissue found in the lower abdomen. Often forming or becoming redundant after rapid weight loss, this fat pad can be susceptible to inflammatory changes. In conditions such as deep morphea—a form of localized scleroderma that affects deeper tissues—the abdominal panniculus may become inflamed or even sclerotic as part of the disease process.
